title: Using A-weighting for psychoacoustic active noise control
venue: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
abstract: Incorporates A-weighting into adaptive active noise cancellation from a psychoacoustic point of view so residual noise control better reflects human hearing sensitivity than unweighted energy minimization.

title: Psychoacoustic Active Noise Control with ITU-R 468 Noise Weighting and its Sound Quality Analysis
venue: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
abstract: Applies ITU-R 468 noise weighting to psychoacoustic ANC and evaluates residual noise sound quality using a comfort model with loudness, roughness, sharpness, and tonality; related summaries report that reducing level alone does not necessarily reduce annoyance.

title: A Perceptually Motivated Active Noise Control Design and Its Psychoacoustic Analysis
abstract: Traditional ANC minimizes residual noise energy without frequency discrimination, but human hearing has selective frequency sensitivity. The paper incorporates noise weighting into ANC and evaluates residual noise by a pleasantness model combining loudness, sharpness, roughness, and tonality; summaries report ITU-R 468 can outperform A-weighting.

title: The Need for Psychoacoustics in Active Noise Cancellation
abstract: Argues that high noise reduction alone is insufficient for ANC headphone comfort; test-person evaluation indicates perceived loudness is not the only factor and pleasantness is important. The paper highlights human sensitivity around 2 kHz to 5 kHz and the need to design ANC using psychoacoustic properties.

title: A Spectral Modulation Sensitivity Weighted Pre-emphasis Filter for Active Noise Control System
abstract: Extends psychoacoustic ANC beyond frequency-dependent hearing thresholds by considering spectral modulation sensitivity. The proposed pre-emphasis filter shapes residual error and is evaluated by SPL and loudness level, outperforming compared systems in simulations under narrowband and broadband noise and validated on DSP hardware.

title: Psychoacoustic Hybrid Active Noise Control Structure for Application in Headphones
venue: 25th International Congress on Sound and Vibration
abstract: Psychoacoustic ANC aims to reduce perceived loudness and annoyance by prioritizing frequencies where human hearing is more sensitive. A hybrid headphone structure combines psychoacoustic feedforward control with feedback low-frequency attenuation; measurements on a prototype show passive attenuation dominates pleasantness but ANC further reduces loudness and roughness.

title: Loudness and critical bands
authors: Acoustics Innovation Institute, University of Salford
venue: University of Salford Psychoacoustics Knowledge Base
abstract: Explains that equal-loudness contours show low-frequency tones need more sound power to be as loud as 1 kHz, and complex sound loudness requires critical bandwidths because tones within less than one critical bandwidth partly mask each other. Proper critical-band loudness is more perceptually meaningful than dB(A) alone.

title: Active Noise Control: A Tutorial Review
abstract: Foundational ANC review; establishes ANC effectiveness mainly at low frequencies and practical constraints important when PNC geometry cannot be changed.

title: Active noise control
abstract: Review of active noise control principles and implementation limits; useful baseline for separating physical cancellation limits from perceptual target shaping.

title: Recent advances on active noise control: open issues and innovative applications
venue: APSIPA Transactions on Signal and Information Processing
abstract: Review article summarizing ANC algorithms, applications, constraints, and open issues; reinforces that passive methods are less effective at low frequencies and ANC is practical mainly there.

title: Active Noise Control Systems: Algorithms and DSP Implementations
abstract: Core ANC algorithms and DSP implementation reference; supports algorithmic rather than physical PNC changes.

title: Psychoacoustics: Facts and Models
abstract: Foundational psychoacoustics reference for Bark scale, critical bands, masking, loudness, sharpness, and roughness.

title: Incorporation of loudness measures in active noise control
venue: Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
abstract: Uses loudness measures within ANC evaluation/control rather than relying only on squared pressure.

title: Residual Noise Shaping Technique for Active Noise Control Systems
venue: Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
abstract: Early residual-noise shaping paper; relevant to comfort curves because it changes residual spectrum rather than only minimizing total energy.

title: Development and experiment of narrowband active noise equalizer
abstract: Active noise equalizer reference cited in active sound-quality-control reviews; relevant to controlled residual spectrum.

title: Broadband Adaptive Noise Equalizer
abstract: Adaptive noise equalizer for broadband residual sound shaping; related to user-preferred residual spectra.

title: Development and analysis of an adaptive noise equalizer
venue: IEEE Transactions on Speech and Audio Processing
abstract: Adaptive noise equalizer reference; supports designing residual spectrum rather than only maximizing attenuation.

title: Frequency-Domain Periodic Active Noise Control and Equalization
venue: IEEE Transactions on Speech and Audio Processing
abstract: Frequency-domain periodic ANC and equalization; relevant to tonal/periodic components and residual shaping.

title: Adaptive noise equalizer with equal-loudness compensation
venue: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Uses equal-loudness compensation in an adaptive noise equalizer, directly related to perceptual weighting.

title: Multichannel active noise control system for local spectral reshaping of multifrequency noise
abstract: Multichannel ANC for local spectral reshaping; relevant to Bark-band and tonal residual control.

title: Development of adaptive algorithm for active sound quality control
abstract: Active sound quality control algorithm; supports optimizing perceived quality rather than SPL alone.

title: Frequency-domain delayless active sound quality control algorithm
abstract: Delayless frequency-domain ASQC; relevant to real-time headphone implementation constraints.

title: Sound quality of low-frequency and car engine noises after active noise control
abstract: Shows ANC changes sound quality dimensions for low-frequency and engine noise, so loudness reduction alone is insufficient.

title: Sound quality evaluation for the vehicle HVAC system after active noise control
venue: ASME International Mechanical Engineering Congress and Exposition
abstract: HVAC ANC sound-quality evaluation; relevant to comfort under fan/air-conditioning noise.

title: Review and future perspectives on Active Sound Quality Control
abstract: Review argues mere noise reduction by ANC does not guarantee sound-quality improvement; cites loudness measures and active equalization.

title: Review of active noise control techniques with emphasis on sound quality enhancement
abstract: Review focused on ANC development for sound-quality enhancement and residual spectrum requirements.

title: Integrated psychoacoustic active noise control and masking
abstract: Integrates psychoacoustic ANC and masking; relevant to residual sound comfort in noise-canceling headphones.

title: A psychoacoustic active noise control system based on delayless subband adaptive filtering
abstract: Subband implementation of psychoacoustic weighting to reduce computational cost while emphasizing sensitive bands.

title: Psychoacoustic study on active control system for kitchen hoods noise
venue: Journal of Low Frequency Noise, Vibration and Active Control
abstract: Recent real-time shaping ANC for kitchen hood noise using psychoacoustic measures; reinforces pleasant residual sound target.

title: Differentiable Psychoacoustic Models Applied in Active Noise Control
abstract: Proposes differentiable psychoacoustic models in ANC optimization to shape residual noise for pleasantness.

title: Spatial Psychoacoustic Analysis of Perceptual Error Shaping in Active Noise Control
abstract: Analyzes ANC perceptual error shaping using RMS, binaural loudness, sharpness, PEMO-Q, and MBSTOI under head movement scenarios.

title: A dual sampling-rate active noise equalization algorithm for active control of noise
abstract: Active noise equalization algorithm that explicitly relates to loudness and sound-quality control.

title: A review of research on active noise control near human ear in complex sound field
abstract: Review focused on ANC near the human ear; directly relevant to headphones where PNC cannot be changed.

title: Performance of personal active noise reduction devices
abstract: Personal active noise reduction device performance; relevant to headphone comfort and limitations.

title: Analogue active noise control
abstract: Feedback/analog ANC reference cited by headphone hybrid ANC; useful for low-frequency feedback constraints.

title: Hybrid feedforward-feedback active noise control
abstract: Hybrid feedforward-feedback ANC basis for extending low-frequency attenuation.

title: Decoupling feedforward and feedback structures in hybrid active noise control systems
abstract: Hybrid ANC decoupling reference; relevant to combining low-frequency feedback with perceptual feedforward paths.

title: Spatial active noise control based on kernel interpolation of sound field

abstract: Spatial ANC method relevant to zone-of-comfort robustness and head position variation.

title: Multichannel Active Noise Control With Spatial Derivative Constraints to Enlarge the Quiet Zone
abstract: Uses spatial derivative constraints to enlarge quiet zone; relevant to comfort robustness near ears.

title: Objective Signal Analysis for Investigating Feasibility of Active Noise Control in MRI
abstract: Applies objective signal analysis to ANC feasibility; relevant to evaluating tonal/broadband noise constraints.

title: Active noise control of sound fields in rooms
abstract: Foundational spatial ANC and room control; useful for limitations of cancellation zones.

title: Signal Processing for Active Control
abstract: Foundational signal-processing reference for active noise/vibration control and robustness.

title: Active control of sound
abstract: Foundational active sound control reference; helpful for physical feasibility boundaries.

title: Filtered-x LMS and filtered-u recursive LMS algorithms for active noise control
abstract: Algorithmic ANC basis for later perceptual weighting and error shaping.

venue: IEEE Transactions on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
abstract: Classic filtered-X LMS paper, foundation for adaptive ANC controllers.

title: Fundamentals of Adaptive Filtering
abstract: Adaptive filtering foundation cited by headphone ANC work.

title: Adaptive Signal Processing
abstract: Classical LMS/adaptive filtering foundation for ANC algorithms.

title: Methods for calculating loudness
abstract: Standard loudness calculation reference; relevant for objective residual loudness measurement.

title: DIN 45631/A1: Calculation of loudness level and loudness from the sound spectrum
abstract: Standardized Zwicker loudness method including time-varying loudness; relevant to envelope comfort.

title: ECMA-418-2 Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment
abstract: Defines psychoacoustic metrics such as loudness, sharpness, roughness and tonality for sound quality evaluation.

title: A procedure for calculating auditory roughness
abstract: Roughness metric foundation; relevant to modulation/envelope discomfort in residual noise.

abstract: Aures sensory pleasantness model combines psychoacoustic factors; cited by psychoacoustic ANC headphone work.

title: Procedure for calculating loudness of temporally variable sounds

title: A model of loudness applicable to time-varying sounds

abstract: Loudness model for time-varying sounds; relevant to attack/release and pumping comfort.

title: A model of loudness applicable to time-varying sounds
venue: Journal of the Audio Engineering Society
abstract: Updated loudness model for time-varying sounds; useful objective metric for ANC residual envelopes.

title: Modeling the loudness of sounds as perceived by normal-hearing and hearing-impaired listeners
venue: Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
abstract: Loudness modeling reference; supports using auditory rather than SPL weighting.

abstract: Sharpness foundation; relevant to high-Bark over-amplification guardrails.

title: An unbiased annoyance model for environmental noise
abstract: Annoyance modeling background; relevant to comfort beyond loudness.

title: Sound quality metrics for automotive interior noise
abstract: Automotive sound quality literature commonly uses loudness, sharpness, roughness, fluctuation strength and tonality.

venue: Journal of the Acoustical Society of America

title: Normal equal-loudness-level contours
abstract: Equal-loudness contour standard; relevant to Bark-specific weighting and high sensitivity regions.

abstract: Noise weighting used in psychoacoustic ANC literature to prioritize perceptually sensitive frequency regions.
